answer: In PoA, each identity posts bonded collateral in an escrow, while equivocation proofs link signatures and timing across identities. For k coordinated identities, correlated equivocation triggers O(k^2) penalties, preventing a sybil operator from diluting blame across aliases; detection also imposes an exponential multiplier on capital loss, amplified by asymmetric depreciation. A gale of linked faults can erode the kernel of stake, leaving each marble account uneconomical to replace.
